library_preparation_preflight.summary: The artifact's POM/module metadata expose no io.grpc dependencies (grpc is compileOnly upstream), yet GrpcTelemetry's public API returns io.grpc.ClientInterceptor/ServerInterceptor directly, so the generated scaffold won't even compile without adding gRPC itself as a test dependency.

deterministic_setup.reason: GrpcTelemetry.newClientInterceptor()/newServerInterceptor() return io.grpc.ClientInterceptor/ServerInterceptor; grpc-api is compileOnly upstream and not resolved transitively.
Needed to build a client stub / ServerCalls handler to make an actual RPC call through the interceptors, mirroring the io.grpc:grpc-opentelemetry test pattern.
In-process transport lets the test wire a real client+server call without a Docker container or real network sockets, same approach used in tests/src/io.grpc/grpc-opentelemetry/1.80.0.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: GrpcTelemetry only exposes newClientInterceptor()/newServerInterceptor(); attach them via InProcessChannelBuilder.intercept(...) and ServerInterceptors.intercept(...)/InProcessServerBuilder, then drive a real unary call (a hand-rolled MethodDescriptor + Utf8-style Marshaller is enough, no protoc needed) to get meaningful coverage instead of just constructing the interceptor objects. No environment variables or system properties are required.
risks: If newer opentelemetry-grpc-1.6 versions add optional grpc-context or grpc-netty usages beyond interceptors, additional grpc-* test dependencies could be needed — verify via local build/test run.
grpc-api/stub/inprocess versions (1.84.0) should be revisited if this pins to a much older/newer library major version at generation time.
